notes: RSS sampled every 5000 inserts and phase boundaries, not a high-frequency peak. Kernel getrusage also records the absolute process lifetime RSS peak on Unix. Timing vectors and test harness included. Synthetic SQL is 117-122 bytes with four profiles and successful executions; count retention is raised to 110000 only for the 100k working-set benchmark. Short queries scan at most 5000 candidate rows per cursor. Migration runs in a fresh process with no previous database, but JSONL is in OS cache. Cold storage-device cache was not flushed. Separate insert_with_spawn_blocking includes dispatch overhead; all timings exclude unchanged star/settings writes. Idle CPU is measured for the store without an app window or live DB drivers, at ps CPU-time resolution (0.01 s). New date-range measurements use profile-0, since one day before and until one day after the run, on 102000 history rows; the FTS and short-query cases first restrict the candidate window to 5000 date/profile-matching IDs. The pinned-first page case uses 400 snippets, 134 pinned, and returns 100 pinned items. Ordering revisions persist in SQLite so cursors survive reopen.
reproduce_command: AXDB_LIBRARY_BENCH_REPORT="$PWD/bench/library-bench-results.json" CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 cargo test -p axdb --lib --release library::tests::library_benchmark --offline -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1

command_contract_notes.history_list: Original array shape plus id; text and error limited to 1024 Unicode characters each; limit capped at 200.
command_contract_notes.history_delete: Existing timestamp/profileName/text camelCase arguments remain accepted; id is the alternative. Legacy deletion also accepts the bounded SQL shown to old clients.
command_contract_notes.new_commands: New multiword arguments use snake_case. history_search and snippet_list return {items,next_cursor}; a short-query cursor can be present on an empty page so callers can continue to older windows.
command_contract_notes.full_text: history_get and snippet_get return full bodies.
command_contract_notes.retention: Default 50000 history rows, 180 days; prune at first use and every 256 inserts in batches up to 512 count-expired and 512 age-expired rows; no idle work.
command_contract_notes.snippet_list: Pinned DESC, updated_at DESC, id DESC; next_cursor is an opaque string passed unchanged as before_id, including snapshot revision and full sort key. Integer legacy cursors return a fixed Query error asking the caller to restart. Ordering is snapshot-isolated across pin and timestamp edits; content/filter membership and deletion are live, and newly inserted snippets are excluded.
command_contract_notes.history_search: Optional RFC3339 since inclusive and until exclusive, with offsets normalized to UTC and nanosecond-precise UTC timestamp boundaries; malformed timestamps and reversed ranges return fixed Query errors. Existing timestamp/profile timestamp indexes bound the candidate window before date-filtered FTS/short matching; scan cursors may accompany empty pages.

unmeasured_limits: True cold storage-device cache: migration uses a fresh process, but its JSONL input is in OS cache.
Full desktop-app CPU/RSS and the existing query-usage settings write are outside the store benchmark.
Latency for large/heterogeneous SQL bodies and all filter combinations was not benchmarked; large-body response bounds and exact gets are covered by tests.
UI, desktop integration, and the inline API argument/result types in ui/src/api.ts are outside this backend-only task; only contract.ts types were added.
Long-term snippet ordering revision growth under sustained edits has not been stress tested; historical sort keys are retained for durable snapshot cursors.
Stored history timestamps are produced in UTC RFC3339 by existing writers; heterogeneous legacy stored timezone offsets were not normalized or benchmarked.
